question: Why can an additional locally legal shape displace a globally feasible construction?

observed_divergence.interpretation: Area-first ranking prioritises a slightly smaller local rectangle despite a worse estimator. Neither local area nor this estimator measures future global feasibility. Appending offers preserves indices but not the greedy selection path. The experimental vertical pass remains removed.

powersom face recipe, free bringup_rails, --shape-area-first off

architecture_findings: floorplan_pack.cpp seat ranks local legal hits; optional area-first ranking overrides the estimator winner.
The same shape_area_first option also changes displaced/incoming recovery shape order. These whole-run experiments do not isolate initial selection from recovery ordering.

attempt_shape_replays explores initial-choice prefixes with a finite frontier and preserves all executed receipts, but it does not possess a previously feasible complete plan from a different offer catalog.
refine_screened_incumbent and outline search preserve already screened layouts within their search; this is distinct from retaining a layout across catalog expansion.
build_pcb_model_once's failure-only orientation expansion adds offers and replans; it cannot recover a successful pre-expansion plan if that plan was never constructed in the current invocation.
next_engineering_target: Establish a same-input complete-plan incumbent before expanded-catalog optimisation, or supply a verified same-input incumbent to the search. Compare complete feasible candidates, retain the incumbent on failure, and account for both strategy runs. Do not replace this with a hardcoded historical board or weaker gates. Add a regression where offer expansion changes the greedy winner and would otherwise lose feasibility.
limits: Diagnosis and two failed screens, not an implemented incumbent portfolio or proof of infeasibility. Ranking experiment does not isolate individual effects. No smaller accepted board, timing-speedup claim, default-policy change or fresh full qualification.
